title: Plant Trees You May Never Sit Under
about:
A keynote-driven course from The Platform Nigeria, taught by Affiong Williams, founder and CEO of ReelFruit, the dried-fruit company she built into an industry across more than 1,000 stores and five export markets.

Using the life of a mango tree as its metaphor, the course moves through four stages of building: the planting season, the waiting years, maturity, and the long harvest. The charge is simple and demanding: build for a future you may never see. Make decisions not for this quarter, but for the Nigeria of 2075 and beyond.
benefits:
• Adopt a long-term, 50-year horizon for how you build
  • Make the first and most consequential decision: deciding to plant
  • Survive the waiting years, when the real work happens underground and unseen
  • Build a canopy: a business whose value outgrows you and serves a whole ecosystem
  • Stay resolute so the right people show up, and engage rather than retreat
  • Think in harvests: inherit the fruit of others and leave fruit for those who follow

steps.title: Plant trees you may never sit under

item.content:
Affiong Williams opens with her calling as an entrepreneur: to build something that bears fruit long after she is gone. It is not just for now, it is for the future.

In this lesson

  • The thesis of the talk: plant trees you may never sit under
  • Fourteen years building ReelFruit, charting a path with no map
  • Why she came to build an industry, not just a product

steps.title: The life of a mango tree

item.content:
The mango tree is the whole talk in one picture: one seed, four stages.

In this lesson

  • The four stages: the planting season, the waiting years, maturity, and the long harvest
  • The best time to plant was 20 years ago; the next best time is now
  • The work starts at once, but there is no fruit for the first five years
  • Then a healthy tree can bear fruit for up to 70 years

The charge to Nigerian builders: make decisions for the long term.

In this lesson

  • Build not for this quarter or this decade, but for the Nigeria of 2075 and beyond
  • Build knowing you may never see the full harvest of what you start
  • Why this long-term horizon is the heart of the whole talk

item.content:
The planting season starts with one decision: deciding to plant.

In this lesson

  • Deciding to start is the most consequential choice you make; everything follows it
  • Why Nigerian business is pushed toward short-term thinking
  • The real pressure: an unstable economy where the Naira devalued over 100% five times in 14 years

The horizon you choose changes how you build everything.

In this lesson

  • Short-term and long-term founders build fundamentally differently
  • The cashew-factory story: she said five years, it took ten
  • Accepting the time it truly takes is part of the mindset

steps.title: Honest about the odds, driven by the vision

item.content:
Long-term builders are honest about the odds, and persist anyway.

In this lesson

  • Your work might never pay off; that is the statistical reality
  • Build with optimism that you are seeding the roots of industry that will pay beyond you
  • When no market existed, she decided to keep planting on the strength of the vision

steps.title: Five years of no fruit: the roots go deep

item.content:
For the first five to eight years, a mango tree shows nothing above ground.

In this lesson

  • By year three the tree looks like a dwarf; it is not impressive
  • Underneath, the roots go deep, find water, and anchor against storms
  • The tree is building the internal infrastructure that will hold it as it grows

steps.title: Waiting is not idle: build the market underneath

item.content:
Waiting does not mean being idle. The real work is happening, unseen.

In this lesson

  • Understand the industry and the customer better than anyone
  • Build a distribution network, take risks, and learn from products that fail
  • Traction, track record, and a team: the roots came before the fruit

steps.title: The canopy: when your vision outgrows you

item.content:
At maturity, a mango tree does something beyond producing fruit: it builds a canopy.

In this lesson

  • A canopy can spread about ten metres wide, sheltering people and an ecosystem
  • Her vision expanded from solving youth unemployment to a supply chain across four countries
  • More problems become more opportunities to create impact

steps.title: Destiny helpers: people show up for the resolute

item.content:
She did not build the business alone.

In this lesson

  • Staying resolute to a vision brings the right people around you
  • Friends, family, and investors show up because they see someone executing
  • The divine moments along the way help you get through

It is easy to say: let me just survive, and leave the rest.

In this lesson

  • After seeing the same problems repeat, retreat starts to feel reasonable
  • If you are fortunate enough to survive, be open enough to do more
  • Engage with the problems only you can see; they help the whole ecosystem, not just you

steps.title: Seventy years of fruit: inherit and leave a harvest

item.content:
A well-tended mango tree bears fruit season after season, for decades.

In this lesson

  • A healthy tree can be productive for up to 70 years
  • Farmers who planted 30 to 40 years ago made today's business possible
  • Local fruit grown in Kaduna, Jos and Niger State now sits on shelves across five countries

steps.title: Builders shape the Nigeria of the future

item.content:
Nigeria's tomorrow is decided by what we build today.

In this lesson

  • We shape the country by what we decide to build, and how
  • The youngest population on earth, with millions of young people seeking opportunity
  • One tree is not a forest; a forest begins with one person planting, then more joining

steps.title: The charge: plant trees you may never sit under

item.content:
The closing charge to entrepreneurs.

In this lesson

  • Even against the odds, building for the future is a worthy pursuit
  • A society grows great when old men plant trees in whose shade they will never sit
  • So plant your trees
